name: veterinary_clinic_system_076_weekly_schedule_load_balance
instruction: Produce the weekly schedule load-balance and capacity report for the 7-day inclusive window starting on the episode date (episode date through episode date + 6 days). Consider only appointments whose status is 'scheduled' or 'confirmed' and whose appointment_date falls in that window. For every provider whose role is 'veterinarian', write an ops_reports row (report='weekly_load') with: provider_id, provider_name, the provider's home location_id, appointment_count, scheduled_hours (each appointment is a 30-minute slot, so count / 2.0), unique_patient_count (distinct patients seen by that vet in the window), and busiest_day (the window date with the most appointments for that vet; ties -> earliest date; null if none). For each of the three clinic locations, write an ops_reports row (report='weekly_load_location') with: location_id, location_name, total_appointment_count (all vet appointments at that location in the window), total_scheduled_hours, unique_vet_count (distinct veterinarians with appointments at that location), unique_patient_count, and busiest_day (most appointments at that location in the window; ties -> earliest; null if none). Write one summary row (report='weekly_load_summary') with: total_vet_appointments, total_vet_scheduled_hours, most_loaded_provider_id (highest scheduled_hours; ties -> smallest provider_id), most_loaded_hours, least_loaded_provider_id (lowest scheduled_hours; ties -> smallest provider_id), least_loaded_hours, and load_balance_ratio (round(most_loaded_hours / least_loaded_hours, 2) when least_loaded_hours > 0, otherwise null). The report is idempotent: delete any prior weekly_load rows for this batch before writing.
_max_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session

success_criteria.summary: 8 ops_reports rows (4 weekly_load, 3 weekly_load_location, 1 weekly_load_summary) keyed by batch_code. Every aggregate is recomputed two independent ways (Python over REST rows and SQL GROUP BY) and must agree with the agent's written values. Non-veterinarian providers and non-window/non-scheduled/confirmed appointments are excluded. Canaries on all collections outside ops_reports.

checks.expect: 8 rows: 4 weekly_load, 3 weekly_load_location, 1 weekly_load_summary with exact computed metrics
per-vet and per-location counts/hours/patient counts/busiest_day computed both by raw-row Python and SQL GROUP BY and both must agree with the written rows

hazards: Non-veterinarian staff: the providers table has 9 rows, but only ids 1-4 have role 'veterinarian'; ids 5-6 are vet_tech, 7-8 are kennel_attendant, and 9 is groomer. Including them would produce 9 weekly_load rows instead of 4 and would add zero-appointment rows for the non-clinical staff.

Wrong location_id on per-provider rows: a provider's home location_id comes from the providers table, but a veterinarian can see appointments at multiple locations in the same week. For example, provider id=1 (home location_id=1) has appointments at location_id=2 and location_id=3 in the 2026-09-30 window (appointment ids 120, 128, 149, 200, 212). An agent that copies the appointment's location_id into the provider row will misreport the provider's home location.

Duplicate patients per vet: some patients have more than one appointment with the same veterinarian in the same week (e.g., patient 212 has two appointments with provider 3 in the 2026-09-30 window; patient 204 has two appointments with provider 4). Counting appointments instead of distinct patient_ids overstates unique_patient_count.

Status and date filtering: the data contains 176 'completed' and 66 'no_show' appointments in other weeks; for the actual episode windows the window only contains 'scheduled' and 'confirmed' appointments, but an agent that does not filter by status and window will include wrong rows.
Tiebreak rules: busiest_day must use the earliest date when multiple days have the same appointment count; most/least_loaded_provider_id must use the smallest provider_id when scheduled_hours tie.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Combines per-provider load, per-location capacity, and a practice-level load-balance ratio in one mission. Requires correctly joining appointments to providers, patients, and locations, handling the fact that a vet's home location differs from the locations where their appointments actually occur, and enforcing tiebreak rules. The verifier uses a dual Python/SQL derivation for every aggregate.
